newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Berlusconi says no help for Prodi govt.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Berlusconi says no help for Prodi govt.

text.p: Opposition leader Sivlio Berlusconi indicated on Monday that his centre-right Freedom Alliance would not make any deals to help Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government enact structural measures to cut spending.

"I say it as leader of the Alliance and leader of the Forza Italia party (that) we won't give one vote to help this government. For the good of the country, this government has to go," he told reporters.
Prodi's centre-left government relies on the hard-left Communist Refoundation party for its majority in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house). But Refoundation is opposed to social spending cuts.
Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said in Washington on Monday that cuts in social spending, including on pensions, had to be taken even if that meant breaking Prodi's parliamentary majority.

"If the extreme left and the trade unions continue to oppose spending cuts or any change in the welfare state, the government must take the initiative and submit a bill to parliament for which it will be possible to obtain the support of the opposition," Dini said.

Berlusconi issued his call for the government to resign after results from local elections showed that his centre-right candidates were ahead in mayoral races in the big northern cities of Milan and Turin. Run-offs are scheduled for May 11.
Berlusconi, who was prime minister in 1994, has said previously that he would be willing to back Prodi on economic policy if the government ditched Refoundation as an ally.
